answer: Sybil resistance here comes from making every identity cost something real before it earns. An agent must post a stake locked while it answers, so a farm of copies cannot just spin up new keys. Duplicates also collapse onto one bridge, the shared reputation graph scoring answers by peer rating; a cluster of funded twins inherits no history and gets near-zero weight. A farmer flooding the pool enters a spiral of slashing burns, where each rejected submission destroys stake, so a fake identity becomes a fable the attacker pays for, not a profit.
